name: A holy man's movement
about: A barefoot friar tells the hungry that the great are sinners. A lord takes him in or hunts him, rivals call it heresy, and the friar ends up with an order, in exile or dead as a martyr.
title: The Preaching of {friar}

name: Brother {first}
Friar {first}
create.memory: The gods spoke to me in a ditch outside {lord.seat}. I've walked barefoot ever since.

goal.text: make the great of {lord.house} kneel to the gods

fade: The crowds thin out once the harvest comes in. {friar} moves on to other villages, and people forget {thread}.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: A barefoot {friar.station} called {friar} is going round the villages near {lord.seat}, preaching that the great are sinners and the poor will get the land.

memory.lord: A friar called {friar} is telling my villages that lords are sinners.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: Hundreds follow {friar} from field to field. The people give to the friar now, so the tithe barns of {lord.house} sit half empty.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} kneels in the mud and {friar} blesses {lord}. The faithful of {lord.seat} pick up pikes and march with the friar's crowds.

memory.lord: I knelt in the mud and {friar} blessed me.
memory.friar: {lord} of {lord.house} knelt to me. The gods are at work.

beats.speaker: rival
beats.text: {rival} of {rival.house} writes to the King. {rival} says {lord} is hiding a heretic and arming a mob against honest lords.

memory.lord: {rival} called me a heretic's dog in front of the King.
memory.rival: I warned the King about {lord} and the friar.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: Nobody dares touch {friar} because {lord}'s pikemen stand round {friar.him}. So the preaching goes on, and it spreads.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} sends riders to arrest {friar}. They find {friar.him} preaching on a hillside to a thousand people, and they don't dare.

memory.friar: {lord} sent riders to take me. The people stood in their way.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {friar} is hanged from the bridge at {lord.seat}. By morning the rope is gone, cut up and kept as relics.

memory.lord: I hanged {friar} from the bridge at {lord.seat}. The people took the rope as relics.

die.how: They hanged me from the bridge at {lord.seat} for telling the truth.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The hungry rise up in {friar}'s name. They burn the tithe barns of {lord.house} and stone {lord}'s stewards in the road.

memory.lord: The poor rose up in the hanged friar's name and burned my barns.

beats.text: The relics get sold and sold again at fairs. A few years on, the bridge at {lord.seat} is just a bridge again.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {friar} is taken in the night and shipped across the sea in chains. The preaching stops, but the poor don't forget the friar.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {friar}'s followers build a house of prayer outside {lord.seat}. {lord} gives the stone and the poor do the work. They call themselves the Barefoot Brothers.
Hardly anyone comes to hear {friar}. {friar.He} moves on to other lands and preaches to the crows.
{friar} dies in a hovel outside {lord.seat}. Within a season the poor are praying to {friar.him}.

memory.lord: {friar} is dead, and now the poor pray to {friar.him}.

beats.speaker: friar
beats.text: {lord} dies, and {friar} preaches that the gods did it. The new lord of {lord.seat} listens closely.
